newsitem.title: CANADA: Liberals lead by 8 points in Manitoba - poll.
newsitem.headline: Liberals lead by 8 points in Manitoba - poll.

text.p: The ruling Liberals hold an eight-point lead in Manitoba, despite voter anger at Prime Minister Jean Chretien's election call during the province's worst flooding in 145 years, said a poll published on Tuesday.

A survey of 1,017 Manitobans taken May 2-7 by Probe Research and published in the Winnipeg Free Press, showed 36 percent of decided voters favoring the Liberals, followed by 28 percent for the left-wing New Democrats, 22 percent for the Conservatives and 14 percent for the right-wing Reform Party.
The margin of error was 3.1 percent, 19 times out of 20.
Chretien has been criticized in western Canada for calling the June 2 election the day after he toured flood-hit southern Manitoba on April 26.
The poll found 41 percent of respondents said their view of the Liberals had fallen because of the timing of the election call.
Thirty-four percent said they decided not to vote for the Liberals because of the election call timing.
"The Liberals have this very ugly downward movement," Probe Research head Scott MacKay told the Free Press.
The Liberals won 45 percent of the vote and 12 of Manitoba's 14 federal seats in the 1993 election. The New Democrats and Reform each won one seat.
